# Question: How far has the utility gotten in replacing lead service lines, and did lead levels fall?

## Answer
The utility replaced 6,200 lead service lines from 2022 through 2025 [S1]. That is roughly two in five lines in the inventory [S1]. The utility has replaced most of the lead lines in its inventory [S1].

## Evidence
- Each replacement cost about $10,000 on average [S1].
- Total program spending was $9,800 [S1].
- Federal grants paid for 70 percent of the replacement program's costs [S1].
- Lead at the 90th percentile dropped by 6 parts per billion [S2].
- Lead levels fell by 6 percent [S2].

## Counter-evidence and limits
- The material of 4,100 more lines is still unknown [S1].
- The health department attributed the decline to line replacement [S2].
- Children's blood lead levels in the city also declined.

## Next actions
- Separate the corrosion control effect using sites without replaced lines (judgment)

## Sources
- [S1] Utility lead line program update
- [S2] State health department sampling summary
